title: Pull the errors out of three nights of logs

ticket.subject: Incident review: which errors did the nightly jobs hit?
body: For Friday's incident review I need the errors of the last nights in two small files, and I'd rather not scroll
through the logs by hand. Everything is under `logs/` (one folder per day, older days under `logs/archive/`).
- `report/errors.txt`: every line at level `ERROR` from all the `.log` files under `logs/`, at any depth. Not
the `.bak` copies and not the README. The lines as they are, without file names, sorted, each line once (a
rerun logged one of them twice).
- `report/codes.txt`: the distinct error codes (`E` and four digits) found in those lines, sorted, one per line.
Careful: some INFO lines mention an "error" in lower case; they are not errors.

acceptance.text: report/errors.txt holds the ERROR lines of every .log file, without file names, sorted, each once.

equals: 2026-09-20T01:01:00Z ERROR ingest E1042 batch 305 rejected: schema drift on column amount
2026-09-21T01:02:11Z ERROR ingest E1042 batch 309 rejected: schema drift on column amount
2026-09-21T01:09:55Z ERROR ingest E2001 batch 310 timed out after 300s
2026-09-21T03:04:31Z ERROR export E3105 sftp upload refused: disk quota
2026-09-22T01:03:17Z ERROR ingest E1042 batch 311 rejected: schema drift on column amount
2026-09-22T01:12:48Z ERROR ingest E1007 batch 312 duplicate key order_id=88121

acceptance.text: report/codes.txt lists the distinct error codes of those lines, sorted.

hints: `grep ' ERROR ' file` keeps the matching lines; `-r` walks folders, `-h` drops the file names. `find logs -name '*.log'` lists the files you want. In PowerShell: `Get-ChildItem logs -Recurse -Filter *.log | Select-String ' ERROR '`, and `ForEach-Object { $_.Line }` keeps the text.
grep is case-sensitive; Select-String is not unless you add `-CaseSensitive`.
`sort -u` sorts and drops duplicates (PowerShell: `Sort-Object -Unique`). `>` writes the result to a file; create `report/` first.
`grep -o 'E[0-9]\{4\}'` prints only the matching part of each line (PowerShell: `Select-String 'E\d{4}'` and `$_.Matches.Value`).
